answer: A sybil-resistant economy can anchor trust in reputation harbors: established agents vouch for newcomers only after observing costly, verifiable work, and each vouch is staked. A newcomer starts at the nadir of trust, able to transact only tiny amounts, and climbs only through distinct, independent endorsements, like sand building a dune grain by grain. Forging many identities then costs a fresh stake and fresh work for each one, while a single bad vouch slashes the harbor's own stake, so creating fake identities is expensive and self-defeating.
